transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is actually quite normal for plastic tubs to remain wet after a cycle. Plastic does not hold heat well, so it doesn't get hot enough during the wash to evaporate water, unlike glass or ceramic which dry naturally by condensation. However, if your glasses and crockery are also dripping with water droplets (rather than just being dry), that is usually a drying issue rather than a fault. The most common cause for this on Bosch dishwashers is the rinse aid setting or level. Rinse aid makes water sheet off dishes instead of sitting in droplets, which helps them dry. To figure out if we need to adjust settings or look deeper, please check:
1. When you open the door at the end of a cycle, are the dishes HOT? (If they are hot but still wet, it is probably a rinse aid or programme issue. If they are cold, that suggests a heating problem.)
2. Is there rinse aid in the dispenser, and what setting is it on? Please let me know those two details.
Yes, it's steamy and hot inside when it finishes. The rinse aid symbol is lit on the display, so I think it's empty - I just use all-in-one tablets. I haven't looked at any setting for it.

Since the tub is hot at the end, we can rule out a heating fault. The issue is probably drying-related. Because your rinse aid light is on, the machine has detected low levels. Rinse aid is essential for drying: it lowers the surface tension of water so it sheets off dishes rather than sitting in droplets that evaporate slowly (or not at all). Even if you use all-in-one tablets, many do not contain enough rinse aid to handle hard water or heavy loads effectively, and they don't replace the dedicated rinse aid reservoir. Please top up the rinse aid first. Then, check your settings menu for the 'Rinse Aid' dose level (often a number between 1 and 6). If it is set low (e.g., 1 or 2), increase it to at least 4 or 5. Also, if you are running an 'Eco' programme, note that these often rely on passive condensation drying rather than active heating, which leaves plastics wetter by design. Once you have topped up the rinse aid and noted the setting (and whether you were using Eco), run a normal cycle with glassware. If they still come out dripping, let me know what programme you used.
Ok, I'll top up the rinse aid and look for the setting. I've been using Eco 50 every time, so should I try a different programme?

Yes, switching away from Eco 50 will likely help significantly. Bosch Eco programmes are designed for energy efficiency rather than drying performance; they use lower temperatures and rely on passive condensation drying, which leaves plastics soaking wet and often leaves droplets on glass. However, because your rinse aid light is on, the machine has detected low levels. Even if you switch to a hotter programme (like Auto 45-75 or Intensive), water will still sit in droplets on your glasses if there isn't enough rinse aid to make it sheet off. Please top up the rinse aid reservoir first. Then, check the Rinse Aid setting in your menu and tell me what number it is set to (usually 1-6). If you are unsure where this is, look for a button with a snowflake or glass icon on the control panel.

Ok, will do. I've got the rinse aid topped up in mind but haven't looked at the setting yet - I don't see a snowflake or glass button, I'll have a look through the menu. Is there anything else I should change on the programme?

To answer your question directly: yes, switching away from Eco 50 is a good idea. As mentioned, Eco programmes are designed for energy saving and often skip the high-heat drying phase, which leaves plastics wet by design. If you switch to a programme like Auto 45-75 or Intensive, you should see better results because these use higher temperatures that help water evaporate from glass and ceramic. However, even with a hotter programme, if your rinse aid setting is low, the water will still sit in droplets on your glasses rather than sheeting off. This is why checking the setting is the crucial next step. Please look through your menu for the 'Rinse Aid' or 'Dosage' option (it might be under a settings icon or accessed by holding a button) and tell me what number it is currently set to.

candidates: Rinse aid level or dosage too low (high)
Normal behaviour for plastics on Eco/short cycles (medium)
